test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 11 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A person buys some bananas at ₹Y per dozen and sells them at ₹(Y)/(4) per banana. What is his gain percentage?
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ CP of 12 bananas = ₹Y SP of 1 banana = ₹Y/4 ⇒ SP of 12 bananas = 12 × (Y/4) = ₹3Y Ratio of CP : SP = Y : 3Y = 1 : 3 Gain = 3 − 1 = 2 units Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (2 ÷ 1) × 100 = 200% **∴ The correct answer is 200%.** **__Alternate Method__** Given: Cost price (CP) of 12 bananas = ₹Y Selling price (SP) of 1 banana = ₹Y/4 Formula Used: Profit % = [(Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP] × 100 CP (12 items) = ₹Y SP (12 items) = ₹3Y • Gain = 3Y − Y = 2Y → Gain % = (2Y/Y) × 100 = 200% ⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) for 12 bananas = ₹Y ⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for 12 bananas = 12 × (Y/4) = ₹3Y ⇒ Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 3Y − Y = 2Y ⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 ⇒ Profit % = (2Y ÷ Y) × 100 ⇒ Profit % = 2 × 100 = 200% **∴ The correct answer is 200%.** **__Additional Information__** Profit Percentage Formula Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It is always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise. Selling Price Calculation SP = CP × [1 + (Gain % ÷ 100)]. This direct formula helps find the final value after a percentage profit. Loss Percentage Formula Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100. A loss occurs when the Cost Price is greater than the Selling Price. e2:T7b2,
